native_result.query: How does age influence the likelihood of withdrawing more money from savings than putting in?
native_result.HypoA: Younger individuals are more likely to withdraw more money from savings than they had put in and with a negative coefficient between age and withdrawing more than putting into savings (-0.0422).
native_result.WorkflowA:
1. One-hot encode Gender variable into MALE and FEMALE
2. Extract the independent variables ['AGE','INCOME', 'BMI', 'BLACK', 'HISPANIC', 'MALE', 'FEMALE']
3. Add dependent variable (DISSAVED) from the df
4. Add a constant term to the independent variable to account for the intercept term in the logistic regression model.
5. Fit a logistic regression model
native_result.HypoB: Among NLSY79 respondents aged 24-32 in 1989, the likelihood of withdrawing more from savings than putting in declines with age: raw rates fall from 25.1% (ages 24-26) to 20.6% (ages 30-32); the primary logit (AGE, AGE_2, log(1+INCOME), GENDER, BMI, BLACK, HISPANIC; HC1 SEs) yields a concave profile peaking near age 25 and falling from ~0.253 at age 24 to ~0.184 at age 32 (~-0.9 pp/yr; joint Wald p<0.001). Excluding SAMESAVE=1 respondents sharpens the decline (0.42 to 0.26). The gradient is directionally robust but magnitude-sensitive to mean-imputed INCOME/BMI rows. Single cohort, one year, ages 24-32 only: no causal or life-cycle claim is supportable.
native_result.WorkflowB: Inspection (missingness, coding, DISSAVED x SAMESAVE cross-tab) -> descriptive age-bin rates with Wilson CIs -> primary logit of DISSAVED on AGE, AGE_2, log(1+INCOME), FEMALE, BMI, BLACK, HISPANIC with HC1 robust SEs -> predicted-probability age profile, marginal effects, turning point -> robustness: SAMESAVE-excluded logit, mean-imputed-row exclusion, imputation flags, linear-in-age logit, BMI>60 exclusion -> joint Wald tests, centered-age stability check, VIF diagnostics -> model-comparison table -> natural-language hypothesis.

sub_hypo.text: Younger individuals are more likely to withdraw more money from savings than they put in, with an age coefficient of -0.0422.
sub_hypo.context: Respondents in the National Longitudinal Survey of Youth (NLSY79) dataset.
sub_hypo.relations: In a logistic regression predicting DISSAVED (1 if withdrawals from savings exceed deposits, 0 otherwise), AGE has a negative coefficient of -0.0422, indicating that younger respondents are more likely to dissave, controlling for INCOME, BMI, BLACK, HISPANIC, and gender encoded as MALE and FEMALE.

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: Younger individuals are more likely to withdraw more money from savings than they had put in and with a negative coefficient between age and withdrawing more than putting into savings (-0.0422).

sub_hypo.text: Among NLSY79 respondents aged 24–32 in 1989, the raw rate of withdrawing more from savings than putting in falls from 25.1% at ages 24–26 to 20.6% at ages 30–32.
sub_hypo.context: NLSY79 respondents aged 24–32 in 1989; a single cohort and one year.
sub_hypo.relations: The raw DISSAVED rate decreases across the stated age bins, from 25.1% to 20.6%.

sub_hypo.text: The primary adjusted logit yields a concave age profile of dissaving, peaking near age 25 and falling from approximately 0.253 at age 24 to 0.184 at age 32, approximately −0.9 percentage points per year; the joint age-term Wald test has p<0.001.
sub_hypo.context: NLSY79 respondents aged 24–32 in 1989; primary logit with HC1 robust standard errors. This single-cohort, single-year association supports neither causal nor life-cycle claims.
sub_hypo.relations: DISSAVED has a concave adjusted age profile modeled using AGE and AGE_2, controlling for log(1+INCOME), GENDER coded as FEMALE, BMI, BLACK, and HISPANIC. Predicted probability peaks near age 25 and subsequently declines; the age terms are jointly significant (Wald p<0.001).

sub_hypo.text: Excluding respondents whose savings did not change or who had no savings sharpens the age-related decline in predicted dissaving probability, from approximately 0.42 at age 24 to 0.26 at age 32.
sub_hypo.context: NLSY79 respondents aged 24–32 in 1989, excluding SAMESAVE=1 respondents; robustness logit.
sub_hypo.relations: Excluding SAMESAVE=1 produces a steeper age-related decline in adjusted DISSAVED probability than the primary model.

sub_hypo.text: The age gradient in dissaving is directionally robust, but its magnitude is sensitive to rows with mean-imputed income or BMI.
sub_hypo.context: NLSY79 respondents aged 24–32 in 1989; robustness checks involving exclusion of mean-imputed INCOME/BMI rows and imputation flags.
sub_hypo.relations: The negative age gradient persists directionally, while its estimated magnitude depends on the treatment of mean-imputed INCOME/BMI rows.

Excluding SAMESAVE=1 respondents sharpens the decline (0.42 to 0.26). The gradient is directionally robust but magnitude-sensitive to mean-imputed INCOME/BMI rows.
